# Kyoto Spring Escape for Two Adults

A relaxed 4-day Kyoto plan for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13** with a **JPY 180,000** on-the-ground budget, focused on temples, local food, quiet neighborhoods, and one easy day trip. I’ve kept each day to **no more than 2 major activities** and built in plenty of slow time.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget

| Day | Plan | Estimated Cost for 2 | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Day 1 — Apr 10 | Arrive, settle into a quiet central area, easy walk in Gion / Higashiyama, casual kaiseki or izakaya dinner | JPY 28,000 | Light first day; keep evening flexible |
| Day 2 — Apr 11 | Arashiyama temples and riverside stroll, local lunch, early dinner near Kyoto Station or downtown | JPY 42,000 | Best for a slower temple-and-nature day |
| Day 3 — Apr 12 | Fushimi Inari in the morning, sake district / lunch, then a calm neighborhood afternoon | JPY 36,000 | Start early to avoid crowds |
| Day 4 — Apr 13 | Day trip to Nara or Uji, return to Kyoto for farewell dinner and dessert stop | JPY 44,000 | One easy day trip with low transit stress |

## 4-Day Kyoto Plan

### Day 1: Arrival, Gion, and a Gentle First Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Kyoto, check in, rest, and get oriented in a central area like Kawaramachi, Gion, or near Kyoto Station.
- Afternoon: Slow walk through **Gion and Higashiyama**; keep it to one temple or shrine max if energy allows.
- Food: Try a quiet first-night meal such as **yudofu, tofu set meals, or a small kaiseki dinner**.
- Estimated cost: lodging JPY 18,000–28,000; meals JPY 8,000–12,000; local transport JPY 1,000–2,000.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Temples and Riverside Calm
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Visit **Tenryu-ji** and the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** early, then take a slow riverside walk.
- Afternoon: Optional low-effort stop at **Okochi Sanso Garden** or just enjoy tea and the area’s quieter side streets.
- Food: Have lunch at a soba or tofu restaurant; keep dinner simple near your hotel.
- Estimated cost: lodging JPY 18,000–28,000; meals JPY 10,000–14,000; transit and entry JPY 4,000–6,000.

### Day 3: Fushimi Inari, Sake District, and a Quiet Neighborhood Afternoon
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Morning: Go early to **Fushimi Inari Taisha** and do a partial hike up the torii path, not the full summit unless you feel like it.
- Afternoon: Head to **Fushimi sake district** for a tasting or museum stop, then return for a low-key neighborhood walk in **Demachiyanagi** or **Nishijin**.
- Food: Try local sake-friendly dishes, grilled fish, or a small ramen shop for lunch.
- Estimated cost: lodging JPY 18,000–28,000; meals JPY 10,000–14,000; transit and entry JPY 3,000–5,000.

### Day 4: Easy Day Trip to Nara or Uji
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Take a simple day trip to **Nara** for Todai-ji and Nara Park, or **Uji** for Byodo-in and matcha cafés.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/25/DeerNaraJapan.jpg Alt=Morning: Take a simple day trip to **Nara** for Todai-ji and Nara Park, or **Uji** for Byodo-in and matcha cafés, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Keep the return to Kyoto unhurried; leave space for one final temple, tea stop, or souvenir browse.
- Food: Choose a local specialty lunch — **matcha sweets in Uji** or **Nara-style set meals**.
- Estimated cost: lodging JPY 18,000–28,000; meals JPY 10,000–14,000; transit and admissions JPY 6,000–10,000.

## Budget Breakdown for the Trip

| Category | Estimated Total |
|---|---:|
| Lodging, 3 nights | JPY 54,000–84,000 |
| Meals and drinks | JPY 36,000–54,000 |
| Local transit | JPY 8,000–14,000 |
| Temple/shrine entries and small admissions | JPY 6,000–12,000 |
| Day trip transport and extras | JPY 10,000–16,000 |
| Shopping / buffer | JPY 10,000–20,000 |
| Total | **JPY 124,000–200,000** |

**Recommended target:** aim for about **JPY 165,000–175,000** to stay comfortably under your **JPY 180,000** cap.

## Packing Checklist for Kyoto in Mid-April

### Clothing and Comfort
- Light jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
- 4 days of easy layers: shirts, one warmer layer, comfortable pants
- Compact umbrella or light rain shell
- Socks you can easily remove for temple visits

### Travel Essentials
- Passport and copies of key documents
- IC card or payment card for trains and convenience stores
- Portable charger and charging cable
- Small day bag or crossbody bag
- Reusable water bottle

### Temple and Day-Trip Items
- Modest outfit options for shrine/temple visits
- Tissue pack and hand sanitizer
- Sunscreen and sunglasses
- Light snack for the day trip
- Phone with offline maps

### Nice-to-Have
- Camera or phone tripod for low-light temple shots
- Cash in small denominations
- Foldable tote for souvenirs
- Basic pain relief / blister care items
